name: getnode
doc:
Get the hardware address as a 48-bit positive integer.

The first time this runs, it may launch a separate program, which could
be quite slow.  If all attempts to obtain the hardware address fail, we
choose a random 48-bit number with its eighth bit set to 1 as recommended
in RFC 4122.

changed.text: Universally administered MAC addresses are preferred over locally administered MAC addresses, since the former are guaranteed to be globally unique, while the latter are not.

name: MAX
doc: A special form of UUID that is specified to have all 128 bits set to one according to RFC 9562, §5.10.

name: NAMESPACE_DNS
doc: When this namespace is specified, the name string is a fully qualified domain name.

name: NAMESPACE_OID
doc: When this namespace is specified, the name string is an ISO OID.

name: NAMESPACE_URL
doc: When this namespace is specified, the name string is a URL.

name: NAMESPACE_X500
doc: When this namespace is specified, the name string is an X.500 DN in DER or a text output format.

name: NIL
doc: A special form of UUID that is specified to have all 128 bits set to zero according to RFC 9562, §5.9.

name: RESERVED_FUTURE
doc: Reserved for future definition.

name: RESERVED_MICROSOFT
doc: Reserved for Microsoft compatibility.

name: RESERVED_NCS
doc: Reserved for NCS compatibility.

name: RFC_4122
doc: Specifies the UUID layout given in RFC 4122. This constant is kept for backward compatibility even though RFC 4122 has been superseded by RFC 9562.

name: SafeUUID
doc: An enumeration.

name: safe
doc: The UUID was generated by the platform in a multiprocessing-safe way.

name: unknown
doc: The platform does not provide information on whether the UUID was generated safely or not.

name: unsafe
doc: The UUID was not generated in a multiprocessing-safe way.

name: UUID
signatures: UUID(hex=None, bytes=None, bytes_le=None, fields=None, int=None, version=None, *, is_safe=SafeUUID.unknown)
doc:
Instances of the UUID class represent UUIDs as specified in RFC 4122.
UUID objects are immutable, hashable, and usable as dictionary keys.
Converting a UUID to a string with str() yields something in the form
'12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789abc'.  The UUID constructor accepts
five possible forms: a similar string of hexadecimal digits, or a tuple
of six integer fields (with 32-bit, 16-bit, 16-bit, 8-bit, 8-bit, and
48-bit values respectively) as an argument named 'fields', or a 16-byte
bytes object (with all the integer fields in big-endian order) as an
argument named 'bytes', or a 16-byte bytes object (with the first three
fields in little-endian order) as an argument named 'bytes_le', or a single
128-bit integer as an argument named 'int'.

UUIDs have these read-only attributes:

    bytes       the UUID as a 16-byte bytes object (containing the six
                integer fields in big-endian byte order)

    bytes_le    the UUID as a 16-byte bytes object (with time_low,
                time_mid, and time_hi_version in little-endian byte order)

    fields      a tuple of the six integer fields of the UUID,
                which are also available as six individual attributes
                and two derived attributes. Those attributes are not
                always relevant to all UUID versions:

                    The 'time_*' attributes are only relevant to version 1.

                    The 'clock_seq*' and 'node' attributes are only relevant
                    to versions 1 and 6.

                    The 'time' attribute is only relevant to versions 1, 6
                    and 7.

        time_low                the first 32 bits of the UUID
        time_mid                the next 16 bits of the UUID
        time_hi_version         the next 16 bits of the UUID
        clock_seq_hi_variant    the next 8 bits of the UUID
        clock_seq_low           the next 8 bits of the UUID
        node                    the last 48 bits of the UUID

        time                    the 60-bit timestamp for UUIDv1/v6,
                                or the 48-bit timestamp for UUIDv7
        clock_seq               the 14-bit sequence number

    hex         the UUID as a 32-character hexadecimal string

    int         the UUID as a 128-bit integer

    urn         the UUID as a URN as specified in RFC 4122/9562

    variant     the UUID variant (one of the constants RESERVED_NCS,
                RFC_4122, RESERVED_MICROSOFT, or RESERVED_FUTURE)

    version     the UUID version number (1 through 8, meaningful only
                when the variant is RFC_4122)

    is_safe     An enum indicating whether the UUID has been generated in
                a way that is safe for multiprocessing applications, via
                uuid_generate_time_safe(3).

name: bytes
doc: The UUID as a 16-byte bytes object (containing the six integer fields in big-endian byte order).

name: bytes_le
doc: The UUID as a 16-byte bytes object (with time_low, time_mid, and time_hi_version in little-endian byte order).

name: clock_seq
doc: The 14-bit sequence number. Only relevant to versions 1 and 6.

name: clock_seq_hi_variant
doc: The next 8 bits of the UUID. Only relevant to versions 1 and 6.

name: clock_seq_low
doc: The next 8 bits of the UUID. Only relevant to versions 1 and 6.

name: fields
doc: A tuple of the six integer fields of the UUID, which are also available as six individual attributes and two derived attributes:

name: hex
doc: The UUID as a 32-character lowercase hexadecimal string.

name: int
doc: The UUID as a 128-bit integer.

name: is_safe
doc: An enumeration of SafeUUID which indicates whether the platform generated the UUID in a multiprocessing-safe way.

name: node
doc: The last 48 bits of the UUID. Only relevant to version 1.

name: time
doc: The 60-bit timestamp as a count of 100-nanosecond intervals since Gregorian epoch (1582-10-15 00:00:00) for versions 1 and 6, or the 48-bit timestamp in milliseconds since Unix epoch (1970-01-01 00:00:00) for version 7.

name: time_hi_version
doc: The next 16 bits of the UUID. Only relevant to version 1.

name: time_low
doc: The first 32 bits of the UUID. Only relevant to version 1.

name: time_mid
doc: The next 16 bits of the UUID. Only relevant to version 1.

name: urn
doc: The UUID as a URN as specified in RFC 9562.

name: variant
doc: The UUID variant, which determines the internal layout of the UUID. This will be one of the constants RESERVED_NCS, RFC_4122, RESERVED_MICROSOFT, or RESERVED_FUTURE.

name: version
doc: The UUID version number (1 through 8, meaningful only when the variant is RFC_4122).

name: uuid1
doc:
Generate a UUID from a host ID, sequence number, and the current time.
If 'node' is not given, getnode() is used to obtain the hardware
address.  If 'clock_seq' is given, it is used as the sequence number;
otherwise a random 14-bit sequence number is chosen.

name: uuid3
doc: Generate a UUID from the MD5 hash of a namespace UUID and a name.

name: uuid4
doc: Generate a random UUID.

name: uuid5
doc: Generate a UUID from the SHA-1 hash of a namespace UUID and a name.

name: uuid6
doc:
Similar to :func:`uuid1` but where fields are ordered differently
for improved DB locality.

More precisely, given a 60-bit timestamp value as specified for UUIDv1,
for UUIDv6 the first 48 most significant bits are stored first, followed
by the 4-bit version (same position), followed by the remaining 12 bits
of the original 60-bit timestamp.

name: uuid7
doc:
Generate a UUID from a Unix timestamp in milliseconds and random bits.

UUIDv7 objects feature monotonicity within a millisecond.

name: uuid8
